text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 5.4% today after oil prices dropped sharply on news of diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran. The price decline follows a two-day, 3.4% slide that began when Saudi and Iranian officials met in Tehran to ease regional conflict, signaling reduced risk of a major supply disruption that had pushed crude prices above $116 just four days earlier. Lower oil prices directly squeeze refiner margins—the difference between what they pay for crude and what they can sell refined products for—which is the core driver of their profits.

The broader picture here is the volatility baked into refiner valuations right now: the stock gained $13 (2.9%) on October 26 alone when geopolitical risk was still priced in, then lost that ground and more as the diplomatic path became clearer. With refineries running at a healthy 93% capacity and oil storage near typical levels, the refiner's near-term economics hinge almost entirely on the crude-to-product price spread, which swings sharply on geopolitical headlines like these.
